question.problem:
Given that 
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}],$ 
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(0,0).$
question.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & -{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ -{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,0),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,0)=(-1)\cdot 1-{0}^{2}=-1.
$$
